prompt: A laptop costs 800 dollars. The shop takes 25 percent off, then adds 10 percent tax on the new price. What is the final price?

options.why: 25 percent off 800 leaves 600. Tax of 10 percent on 600 adds 60. The total is 660.
This adds the 10 percent tax to the first price of 800 instead of to the discounted 600.
600 is the price after the discount. The tax has not been added yet.
This takes 25 percent off and then adds 25 percent back, which is not what the question says.

hint: Work the two steps in order. The tax goes on the new price.

options.why: Percent means "out of 100". 240 x 15 / 100 = 36.
That is 10% of 240. The question asks for 15%.
That is 240 divided by 6, which is about 16.7%.
This divides 240 by 15 instead of taking 15 parts out of 100.

hint: Multiply by the percent, then divide by 100.

prompt: A price rises from 80 to 100. By what percent did it rise?

options.why: The rise is 100 - 80 = 20. Compare it with the OLD price: 20 / 80 = 0.25, so 25%.
This divides the rise by the NEW price (20 / 100). Percent change always uses the old one.
That is the new price as a share of the old one. The rise alone is 25%.
This is the old price read as a percent. It is not a change at all.

hint: Change divided by the ORIGINAL value.

prompt: A shop takes 20% off a price, then takes a further 10% off the new price. What single discount equals the two together?

options.why: You pay 80% and then 90% of that: 0.8 x 0.9 = 0.72. You pay 72%, so the discount is 28%.
Discounts do not simply add. The second 10% is taken off a smaller price, so it saves less.
No step gives this. 0.8 x 0.9 is 0.72 exactly.
This is less than the first discount on its own, which cannot be right.

hint: Multiply what you still pay, do not add what you save.

prompt: Share 120 in the ratio 2 : 3. How big is the larger share?

options.why: The ratio has 2 + 3 = 5 parts. One part is 120 / 5 = 24. The larger share is 3 parts, so 72.
That is the smaller share, 2 parts of 24.
That is half of 120. It would be right only for a 1 : 1 ratio.
That is 2 parts out of 3, which ignores the 5-part total.

hint: Add the ratio numbers first. That tells you how many parts there are.

prompt: Boys and girls in a class are in the ratio 3 : 2. There are 15 more boys than girls. How many students are there in all?

options.why: The gap is 3 - 2 = 1 part, and that part is 15 students. The whole class is 3 + 2 = 5 parts, so 5 x 15 = 75.
That is the number of boys only (3 parts). The question asks for everybody.
That is the number of girls only (2 parts).
This treats 15 as the total of the five parts instead of the gap.

hint: How many parts is the DIFFERENCE worth?

prompt: The average of 5 numbers is 18. What do the 5 numbers add up to?

options.why: Average = total / count. Turn it round: total = average x count = 18 x 5 = 90.
This adds 18 and 5. An average is about multiplying, not adding.
This subtracts 5 from 18, which has no meaning here.
This divides 18 by 5. That would shrink the average, not give the total.

subtopic: Average when one value is added
prompt: The average of 4 numbers is 20. A fifth number is added and the average becomes 22. What is the fifth number?

options.why: The new total is 22 x 5 = 110. The old total was 20 x 4 = 80. The new number is 110 - 80 = 30.
Adding a number equal to the old average would leave the average at 20, not raise it.
That is only the rise in the average. The new number must also carry the other four up.
This adds 20 and 22. Work with totals, not with the two averages.

hint: Work out both totals, then subtract.

prompt: A car covers 180 km in 3 hours. What is its speed in km per hour?

options.why: Speed = distance / time = 180 / 3 = 60 km/h.
This multiplies instead of dividing. 540 km is how far it would go in 9 hours.
That would be 180 km in 2 hours.
This divides 180 by 30. The time given is 3 hours, not 30.

prompt: A car drives 60 km at 30 km/h, then drives the same 60 km back at 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?

options.why: Total distance is 120 km. Time out is 60/30 = 2 h, time back is 60/60 = 1 h, so 3 h in all. 120 / 3 = 40.
This is the plain mean of 30 and 60. You cannot average speeds that way, because the slow leg takes longer.
No step gives this. The slow half pulls the answer down below the middle.
This is too low. Check the times: 2 hours and 1 hour, not 2 and 2.

hint: Total distance divided by total time. Never average the two speeds.

prompt: A finishes a job alone in 6 days. B finishes the same job alone in 12 days. Working together, how many days do they need?

options.why: In one day A does 1/6 and B does 1/12, which is 3/12 = 1/4 of the job. So the whole job takes 4 days.
That is the average of 6 and 12. Two workers must be FASTER than either one alone.
This adds the two times. Working together makes the job shorter, not longer.
Faster than half of A alone is not possible, because B is slower than A.

hint: Add what each one does in ONE day.

prompt: A can finish a job in 10 days. He works for 4 days and then stops. What fraction of the job is still not done?

options.why: Each day is 1/10 of the job, so 4 days is 4/10 done. What is left is 6/10, which cuts down to 3/5.
That is the part he FINISHED (4/10). The question asks what is left.
No step gives this. Check that 6/10 cuts down by dividing both numbers by 2.
A fraction of a job cannot be bigger than 1. This compares the two day counts instead of using the whole job.

hint: Find the part done first, then take it away from the whole.

prompt: An item costs 400 to buy and is sold for 500. What is the profit percent?

options.why: Profit is 500 - 400 = 100. Profit percent always compares with the COST: 100 / 400 = 0.25, so 25%.
This divides the profit by the selling price. That is margin, not profit percent.
100 is the profit in money, not a percent.
That is the selling price as a share of the cost. The profit part alone is 25%.

hint: Profit percent is measured against the cost price.

prompt: An item costs 600 and is sold at a loss of 15%. What is the selling price?

options.why: A 15% loss means you get 85% of the cost. 600 x 0.85 = 510.
That is a 15% GAIN. A loss makes the price go down.
That takes away 15, not 15 percent. 15% of 600 is 90.
That is the loss in money, not the price you sell at.

hint: If you lose 15%, what share of the cost do you still get?

prompt: Find the simple interest on 5000 for 3 years at 8% per year.

options.why: Simple interest = principal x rate x time / 100 = 5000 x 8 x 3 / 100 = 1200.
That is one year of interest. The money sits for 3 years.
That is the principal plus the interest. The question asks for the interest only.
No step gives this. 8% of 5000 is 400, and 400 x 3 is 1200.

hint: Simple interest is the same amount every year.

prompt: 2000 is invested at 10% per year, compounded once a year. What is the total amount after 2 years?

options.why: Each year the money is multiplied by 1.1. 2000 x 1.1 x 1.1 = 2420.
That is simple interest: 200 twice. Compounding also pays interest on the first year’s interest.
That is after one year only.
That is the interest alone. The question asks for the total amount.

hint: Year two earns interest on year one’s interest too.

prompt: A bag holds 4 red balls and 6 blue balls. One ball is taken out without looking. What is the probability that it is red?

options.why: There are 4 red out of 4 + 6 = 10 balls. 4/10 cuts down to 2/5.
This compares red with blue. Probability compares one outcome with ALL outcomes.
That is the chance of blue, which is 6/10.
The 4 is the count of red balls, not the number of equally likely groups.
